chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb and others from our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a believing man who marries a Jewish woman or a Christian woman. He said: “If he has access to a Muslim woman, then what would he do with a Jewish woman or a Christian woman?”

I said: “He may be inclined toward her.” He said: “If he does so, then he must prevent her from drinking wine and eating pork, and know that in his religion there is a diminishment in his marrying her.”

key_terms.غَضَاضَةً: a diminishment, deficiency, or lowering in religious standing
key_terms.ٱلْمُؤْمِنِ: the believing man; a Muslim characterized by faith

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say about a Muslim man marrying a Jewish or Christian woman?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling and disapproval concerning a believing Muslim man marrying a Jewish or Christian woman when a Muslim woman is available. It indicates that if such a marriage occurs, he must restrain her from openly consuming wine and pork, and that such a marriage entails a diminishment in his religious standing.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4422 - And Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Muawiyah ibn Wahb and others of our companions, from Abu Abdullah (as).
He said: I asked Imam (as) about a believing man marrying a Jewish or Christian woman.
Imam (as) replied: "If he has access to a Muslim woman, what need does he have for a Jewish or Christian woman?"
I said: "He may have affection for her."
Imam (as) said: "If he does so, then he must prevent her from drinking wine and eating pork, and know that there is a deficiency in his religion for marrying her."
